title: Secrets and supply chain review
summary: Find credentials in code, logs and evidence, and review dependency and install-time execution risk before a change adds a package or a script.

provenance.notes: Matches this repository's rules: no new dependencies in delegated tasks, npx --no-install only, and credentials never persisted in evidence.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Credential exposure and dependency risks, with the location of each.

workflow.step: Scan the diff and touched files for credential shapes: private keys, bearer tokens, cloud keys, high-entropy assignments in config.
workflow.check: Matches are reported by location only; never repeat the secret value.

workflow.step: Check logging, error messages, test fixtures and evidence records for values that originated in credentials.
workflow.check: Credentials cannot leave through logs or artifacts.

workflow.step: Inspect dependency changes: new packages, version ranges, install scripts, packages fetched at run time.
workflow.check: Each new dependency has a stated reason and a pinned version.

workflow.step: Check that commands never fetch code at run time (npx without --no-install, curl piped to a shell).
workflow.check: Execution uses only already-installed, pinned tools.

workflow.step: For each finding recommend the removal or rotation step, and a test or scan that will catch a recurrence.

constraints: Never print, copy or store a discovered secret; report file and line only.
Do not install or run an unfamiliar package to inspect it.
A delegated task may not add dependencies; report the need instead.

examples.title: Token in test fixture
examples.situation: A fixture contains a string shaped like a GitHub token.
examples.guidance: Report the file and line, recommend replacing it with an obvious fake, and add a scan to the test suite.

verification: No secret value appears in the report.
Every dependency change is accounted for.

task.text: Review the diff for a leaked api key or token in logs and a new dependency in package.json.
Check the go.mod supply chain and any postinstall style install script risk.
